facts.statement: The genus Astorgosuchus was established by Martin and colleagues in 2019.
facts.quote: authority: Martin et al., 2019

facts.statement: Astorgosuchus is estimated to have reached lengths of up to 7 to 8 meters.
facts.quote: This crocodile may have reached lengths of up to 7 - 8 m

facts.statement: Bite marks found on juvenile Paraceratherium bones are attributed to a large crocodile, but it is uncertain if Astorgosuchus made them.
facts.quote: Bite marks of a large crocodile have been found on the bones of juvenile Paraceratherium, however if these were left by Astorgosuchus cannot be said with certainty

facts.statement: The first crocodilian remains from the Bugti Hills were described by G. E. Pilgrim in 1908 and 1912.
facts.quote: The earliest described crocodilian remains from the Bugti Hills of Pakistan were described by G. E. Pilgrim in 1908 and 1912

facts.statement: The type species was originally named Crocodylus bugtiensis by Pilgrim in 1908.
facts.quote: Among these remains were those of large tomistomines and a broad-snouted crocodylomorph of exceptional size first named "Crocodylus" bugtiensis in 1908

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IM E221 consists of a left maxilla and cranial fragments found at Pishi Nala and is housed in the Indian Museum in Kolkata.
facts.quote: These remains, holotype specimen IM E221, consisted of a left maxilla with assorted cranial fragments discovered at Pishi Nala, formally described in 1912 and housed in Indian Museum, Kolkata

facts.statement: Additional remains were discovered in Baluchistan in the 1920s and presented to the Natural History Museum in London in 1925.
facts.quote: Further remains were discovered in Baluchistan in the 1920s and presented by Clive Foster-Cooper to the Natural History Museum, London in 1925

facts.statement: A maxilla fragment reported by K. N. Prasad was found on Piram Island in western India and dated to the Late Miocene.
facts.quote: Later K. N. Prasad reported a maxilla fragment from Late Miocene aged Piram Island of western India

facts.statement: Martin and colleagues formally created the genus Astorgosuchus in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019, Martin et al. created the genus Astorgosuchus

facts.statement: The genus name Astorgosuchus combines Greek words meaning merciless and crocodile.
facts.quote: The name Astorgosuchus derives from the Greek "Astorgos", meaning merciless or inexorable, and "Souchos", meaning crocodile

facts.statement: The species name bugtiensis refers to the Bugti Hills in Pakistan.
facts.quote: The species name refers to the Bugti Hills of Pakistan

facts.statement: Astorgosuchus is described as a large-bodied crocodyloid with a blunt snout.
facts.quote: Astorgosuchus is inferred to have been a large bodied, blunt-snouted crocodyloid

facts.statement: Skull lengths for specific specimens are estimated at 80 to 91 centimeters.
facts.quote: The skull length has been estimated to be around 80 to 91 cm for UM-DB-LCJ1-01 and NHMUK R.5266, respectively

facts.statement: The snout of Astorgosuchus was short and broad, measuring only twice as long as it was wide.
facts.quote: Astorgosuchus had a short and broad snout, being only twice as long as wide

facts.statement: The fifth maxillary tooth is the largest tooth in the upper jaw.
facts.quote: The 5th maxillary tooth is the biggest tooth of the maxilla

facts.statement: The external nostrils extend further back than in modern crocodilians, reaching the level of the fifth maxillary tooth.
facts.quote: The external nares extend much further posteriorly than in modern crocodilians, reaching as far back as the enlarged 5th maxillary tooth

facts.statement: The side of the lower jaw bone is heavily ornamented with deep circular holes.
facts.quote: The lateral surface of the dentary is profusely ornamented with deep circular foramina

facts.statement: The third, fourth, and fifth lower teeth are adjacent, with the fourth being the largest.
facts.quote: The 3rd, 4th and 5th dentary teeth are contiguous with the 4th being the largest dentary tooth

facts.statement: Astorgosuchus lived in the Bugti Hills of Balochistan, Pakistan, during the late Oligocene.
facts.quote: Astorgosuchus is an extinct monospecific genus of crocodilian, closely related to true crocodiles, that lived in Bugti Hills of Balochistan, Pakistan during the late Oligocene period

facts.statement: Astorgosuchus inhabited a river and lake environment shared with rhinoceroses, chalicotheres, anthracotheres, and proboscideans.
facts.quote: During the Oligocene, the area Astorgosuchus was found in was a fluvial lacustrine environment it shared with members of Rhinocerotoidea, Chalicotheriinae, Anthracotheriidae and proboscideans

facts.statement: Astorgosuchus is most closely related to the basal crocodyloid Asiatosuchus germanicus.
facts.quote: Astorgosuchus most closely resembles Asiatosuchus germanicus, a basal crocodyloid from the Eocene

facts.statement: The involvement of the splenial in the lower jaw symphysis distinguishes Astorgosuchus from Crocodylinae and Mekosuchinae.
facts.quote: Notably, the fact that the splenial is involved in the mandibular symphysis differentiates Astorgosuchus from members of Crocodylinae and Mekosuchinae

facts.statement: Astorgosuchus belongs to the superfamily Crocodyloidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Crocodyloidea

facts.statement: Astorgosuchus is an extinct archosaurian crocodilian genus closely related to modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: Astorgosuchus es un género extinto de reptil arcosaurio crocodiliano, cercanamente relacionado con los cocodrilos modernos

facts.statement: The time range for Astorgosuchus is from the Rupelian to the Chattian stages, approximately 33.9 to 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Chattian (33.9 to 23.04 million years ago)
